_comment: Maps CodeQL rule IDs to CWE and WMI classifications for spec generation

stailor/wmi-1-stale-reference-creation.klee_strategy: Allocate object, store pointer in second struct, free first object. Assert stale pointer is non-NULL and dereferenceable.
stailor/wmi-1-stale-reference-creation.driver_hint: Create two linked objects. Free the first (referenced) object. The second object's pointer field should still point to freed memory. Make freed memory symbolic to detect reads.

stailor/wmi-1b-stale-reference-incomplet.klee_strategy: Remove object from container, verify back-pointers not cleared.
stailor/wmi-1b-stale-reference-incomplet.driver_hint: Add object to list/table, store direct pointer in another struct. list_del + kfree the object. Verify the direct pointer in the other struct is never nullified.

stailor/wmi-2-type-confusion-leak.klee_strategy: After free, allocate different-typed object in same memory. Read through stale pointer. Assert read value matches new object's field layout.
stailor/wmi-2-type-confusion-leak.driver_hint: Free object A. malloc(sizeof(B)) where sizeof(B)==sizeof(A). Write known value to B's field. Read through stale pointer to A — should see B's data reinterpreted as A's field.

stailor/wmi-3-arbitrary-free-stale-trave.klee_strategy: Set up fake struct at reclaimed memory with controlled pointer fields. Trigger destructor that follows stale pointer, reads fake list, frees controlled address.
stailor/wmi-3-arbitrary-free-stale-trave.driver_hint: Free referenced object. Reclaim with struct containing pointer to target address. Trigger cleanup function that walks the linked structure through stale reference. Verify target address is passed to free().

stailor/wmi-4-write-what-where-reclaim.klee_strategy: After arbitrary free of target, allocate same-size object. Write controlled data. Verify data appears at target address.
stailor/wmi-4-write-what-where-reclaim.driver_hint: Free the target address (e.g., function pointer table). Immediately allocate same-size block. Write attacker-controlled value (e.g., address of win function). Verify the function pointer at target is overwritten.

stailor/kernel-lifecycle-mismatch.klee_strategy: Register subsystem A with object B. Destroy B. Trigger A's cleanup/access path that dereferences stale B pointer.
stailor/kernel-lifecycle-mismatch.driver_hint: Kernel-specific: Create net_device, attach nf_chain to device. Unregister device (triggers kfree). Trigger chain operation that dereferences chain->dev.

stailor/kernel-funcptr-reclaimable-struc.wmi_name: Exploitation Target (Function Pointer in Reclaimable Struct)
stailor/kernel-funcptr-reclaimable-struc.klee_strategy: Informational: identifies structs suitable for WMI-4 reclamation.
stailor/kernel-funcptr-reclaimable-struc.driver_hint: This is an exploitation target, not a standalone vulnerability. After WMI-3 frees an address in this struct's slab cache, reclaim with controlled data to overwrite the function pointer.

full_chain_netfilter.description: CVE-2024-26808 pattern: Netfilter UAF → Leak → Arb Free → WWW → LPE

steps.action: Create nf chain attached to dummy device, delete device
Reclaim device memory with packet_fanout, read chain->dev->name
Reclaim with msg_msg, leak heap/text address
Reclaim device with fake struct, destroy chain → kfree(controlled_addr)
Reclaim freed pipe_buffer, vmsplice to get page address, overwrite core_pattern

generic_uaf_chain.description: Generic UAF exploitation chain for userspace programs

steps.action: Reclaim with different type, leak via type confusion
Fake struct at reclaimed location, trigger cleanup → arbitrary free
Reclaim freed function pointer table, overwrite with target
